execution_safety_defaults._evidence_live_dry_run: Dry-run is the MANDATORY first state after arming and records the real bid/ask at signal time without sending an order. It exists because execution cost is currently unmeasurable: paper fill_price is taken from signal_ltp, so scripts/report_slippage.py reads a constant zero no matter how many fills accumulate. UNIT CORRECTION: the two standing assumptions were previously described as 4x apart, which was wrong - they are quoted in different units. simulated_slippage_pts mean 0.125 pts = Rs8.13 is PER LEG (Rs16.26 per round trip); the backtests' SLIPPAGE_INR_PER_TRADE = 32.50 (0.5 pts) is PER ROUND TRIP. Normalised, the disagreement is 2x, not 4x. Rs32.50 is therefore not an arbitrary constant: it is the round-trip cost of crossing a 0.5-point spread, which is a plausible NIFTY ATM option touch. Which figure is right is still UNMEASURED and is what the dry-run ledger decides. Exit is gated on 30 recorded dry-run orders, NOT on elapsed days, because a day count measures nothing about spread.
execution_safety_defaults._evidence_live_entry_window: New LIVE entries close at 15:05, not 15:30. EOD square-off is 15:20; allowing entries until 15:30 opens a window in which an order is placed and immediately squared off, paying charges both ways for nothing. 15:05 leaves a minimum hold. Paper and dry-run are unaffected - this gates real orders only.
execution_safety_defaults._evidence_live_limits: ARITHMETIC NOTE: these two limits conflict and the LOSS cap always fires first. One 40-point stop on lot 65 = Rs2,600 + ~Rs78 charges = ~Rs2,678, so a Rs5,000 daily loss cap halts trading after TWO losses and the 3-trade cap is never reached. The requested figure was 'Rs5000 or 40 pts x 65 lot', but 40 x 65 is Rs2,600, not Rs5,000. Both values are kept exactly as specified and neither is tuned; this note records that they are not equivalent.
execution_safety_defaults._evidence: Paper and algo-only are unconditional. Current NO-GO prevents real-money opt-in. Any future approved opt-in is session-only and resets OFF at restart.
